domain_reasoning: The time goes into reading the loss report against the policy wording and writing the determination, with little system operation beyond retrieval and recording.
length_reasoning: A clear-cut loss under a standard policy takes about ten minutes; a loss with exclusions, endorsements or ambiguous facts takes over an hour.
review_reasoning: The reviewer opens the file, reads the loss report and the cited policy clauses, and checks the reasoning; complex cases need several clauses and endorsements traced.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong denial or approval reaches the customer and may be reversed, but a wrongful denial can raise complaint or regulatory exposure.
context_reasoning: Needs the insurer's policy forms and claims-handling rules, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into pulling up the policy and account on screen and noting the answer.
length_reasoning: A simple coverage question takes a few minutes; one with exclusions or unclear facts and several lookups takes a quarter hour.
review_reasoning: A quality reviewer listens to the call and checks the answer against the policy and the account note; longer calls take longer to follow.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong answer may lead the customer to rely on coverage that is later denied, causing complaint but no binding decision, since it is stated as appearing covered.
context_reasoning: Needs the insurer's products and phrasing rules, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is reading code and running static analysis or test tooling against the standards, then writing up deviations.
length_reasoning: A small build against a short checklist takes an hour; a large program against a full standard such as accessibility or coding standards takes days of work.
review_reasoning: The lead reads the report and verifies a sample of the deviations in the code; large reviews need many findings confirmed.
stakes_reasoning: Missed deviations are usually found later in testing or review and fixed, though compliance-critical products can face regulatory exposure.
context_reasoning: Needs the applicable standards and the product's code, some of which is public, with a few weeks to learn the codebase.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into diagnosing with remote tools, settings screens and knowledge base and logging the contact.
length_reasoning: A simple how-to takes a few minutes; troubleshooting a persistent fault with the user takes half an hour.
review_reasoning: A supervisor listens to the call and checks the fix and log entry; longer contacts take longer.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong fix wastes the user's time or breaks a setting but is usually reversible and noticed soon.
context_reasoning: Needs the organization's standard software, devices and policies, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Writing test cases means reading requirements and producing structured text; test tools are used mainly for storage.
length_reasoning: A small feature takes an hour; a feature with many rules and integration points takes more than a day.
review_reasoning: The lead reads the cases against the requirements and checks coverage and gaps, which takes a fraction of the writing time.
stakes_reasoning: Gaps in cases are caught later in testing or production and the cost is moderate, with defects escaping for a few features.
context_reasoning: Needs the feature's requirements and the product's behavior, which takes weeks to learn.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into reading and consolidating feedback and writing the report; filing defects is a smaller portion.
length_reasoning: A small test round with a few testers takes an hour; a large round with many feedback items takes a day.
review_reasoning: The product owner reads the report, checks the severities and spot-checks the defect tickets against the feedback.
stakes_reasoning: Misreported or missed defects delay fixes or release decisions but are usually corrected, though a missed severe defect can reach users.
context_reasoning: Needs the product and test round context, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into looking up billing history, usage and weather or rate information on screen.
length_reasoning: A simple bill query takes a few minutes; one needing multi-month usage comparison and explanation takes 20 minutes.
review_reasoning: The reviewer listens to the call and checks the account figures against the explanation given.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong assessment leads to a dispute or complaint and possibly an incorrect adjustment, which can be reversed.
context_reasoning: Needs the utility's tariffs, billing system and complaint rules, learned over weeks.

unit_flag_reason: Customizations range from a template tweak to a scripted macro, mixing very different kinds of work.
domain_reasoning: Macros, scripts, templates and configuration are code or configuration changes plus testing.
length_reasoning: A small template tweak takes half an hour; a macro or configuration needing scripting and testing takes two days.
review_reasoning: The supervisor reviews the change and test results; larger scripts need reading and trial runs.
stakes_reasoning: A faulty customization reaches users and causes rework, but can generally be rolled back; a few affect critical processes.
context_reasoning: Needs the internal processes and the specific commercial program, learned over weeks.

unit_flag_reason: Scope runs from a small helper script to a full framework component, mixing very different amounts and kinds of work.
domain_reasoning: Building a testing tool is writing and testing code.
length_reasoning: A small helper script takes half a day; a framework component with review and adoption takes weeks.
review_reasoning: A reviewer reads the code, runs it and checks documentation; larger components take hours.
stakes_reasoning: Bugs in test tooling cause false results that are noticed by the team and fixed, though they can hide product defects.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's stack, conventions and product, learned over weeks to months.

domain_reasoning: The time goes into using diagnostic tools, admin consoles and remote sessions on the user's machine and the ticketing system.
length_reasoning: A routine fix takes ten minutes; an obscure fault needing research and several attempts takes three hours.
review_reasoning: The lead reads the ticket and notes and checks the fix and the user confirmation; hard cases need the chain of steps followed.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong fix leaves the user unresolved or causes rework, usually reversible; a few cases affect security or data.
context_reasoning: Needs the organization's environment, standard builds and escalation paths, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Writing a suite means reading specifications and writing structured cases and scripts, mostly as text, with the repository as storage.
length_reasoning: A small area takes two hours; a regression or database-impact suite for a release takes several days.
review_reasoning: The lead reads the suite against the scope and checks coverage and spot-checks cases; large suites take hours.
stakes_reasoning: Gaps allow defects to reach production, with moderate cost, and areas like database impacts can lose data.
context_reasoning: Needs the product's behavior and test repository conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is reading scope and dates and writing a strategy and schedule document, supported by some planning tools.
length_reasoning: A small release takes a couple of hours; a large project plan with risk analysis and negotiations takes days.
review_reasoning: The manager reads the plan, checks estimates and dependencies against scope and dates.
stakes_reasoning: A bad plan causes delays or insufficient testing, discovered gradually, with possible release slips.
context_reasoning: Needs the project's scope, team capacity and organizational process, learned over months.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into executing test steps in the application and test environment and recording results in test and defect tools.
length_reasoning: A small change takes half an hour; a change with many regressions takes two days.
review_reasoning: The release manager reads the results and spot-checks defects and evidence; long cycles need more results verified.
stakes_reasoning: A change signed off incorrectly can reach production and cause outages or errors, depending on the system.
context_reasoning: Needs the system's behavior, test environment and release process, learned over months.

domain_reasoning: The work is gathering tool information, comparing and writing a recommendation, with some trial use of the tools.
length_reasoning: A quick comparison of two tools takes half a day; a formal trial of several tools takes a couple of weeks.
review_reasoning: The manager reads the report and checks the criteria, comparison and any cost claims.
stakes_reasoning: A poor tool choice costs money and rework and is hard to reverse once adopted, though adoption is a manager's decision.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's process, needs and budget, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Preparing the referral means gathering case details from systems and entering them in the referral form or ticket.
length_reasoning: A straightforward case takes five minutes; a long history to summarize takes half an hour.
review_reasoning: The receiving department reads the referral for completeness and checks facts against the case history.
stakes_reasoning: A poor referral causes delay and rework for the customer but is easily corrected.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's departments, referral rules and systems, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Reproducing a problem means running the software, reading logs and sometimes code, and then filing a defect.
length_reasoning: A simple reproducible issue takes half an hour; an intermittent issue needing environment setup takes a day.
review_reasoning: The developer reads the findings and attempts to reproduce using the steps, which takes some time.
stakes_reasoning: Wrong findings cause the customer problem to remain or developers to chase wrong defects, with moderate cost.
context_reasoning: Needs the product and customer configurations, learned over months.

domain_reasoning: The work is writing the problem, steps and outcome into ticket notes, with little other system work.
length_reasoning: A routine note takes a couple of minutes; a long troubleshooting history takes fifteen.
review_reasoning: The lead reads the notes and checks them against the problem; a longer history takes a few more minutes.
stakes_reasoning: Poor records cause minor confusion for later staff and are cheap to fix.
context_reasoning: Needs the ticket categories and conventions, picked up quickly.
